title: Assessing DxGPT: Diagnosing Rare Diseases with Various Large Language Models

paper.authors: do Olmo, Logrono, Mascias, Martinez, Isla (Foundation 29)
paper.repo_commit: c7abe550ccad59465bdf53b67e9629e3f239f0eb (HEAD 2025-01-20; shallow clone external/repos/W4396768794/foundation29org__dxgpt_testing; note: PDF link extraction gave 'dxgpt_testi', real name is dxgpt_testing)
paper.other_artifacts: RAMEDIS and PUMCH cases loaded from Hugging Face dataset chenxz/RareBench (configs 'RAMEDIS', 'PUMCH_ADM', split 'test'); synthetic 200-case set in repo data/synthetic_data_v2.csv

dependence.note: The paper is a benchmark of diagnostic accuracy of 13 LLMs; every number depends on model outputs. Additionally the metric itself is LLM-judged (GPT-4-0613 classifies P1/P5/P0), so the paper has a second, auxiliary 'judge' dependence on a now-dead model. Raw diagnoses and judge scores for every model/dataset are archived in the repo (data/diagnoses_*.csv, data/scores_*.csv) - a strong L1 case.

claim.statement: On the 200 real-world RAMEDIS rare-disease cases (HPO symptom lists), GPT-4 Turbo 0409 (gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09) reaches 54.04% Strict Accuracy (P1) and 68.69% Top-5 Accuracy (P1+P5), i.e. second among closed models behind Claude 3 Opus (55.00/70.00) and ahead of GPT-4 0613 (50.25/63.32) (Table 3, Section 3.1.2).
claim.metric: Strict Accuracy = share of cases whose top-1 suggestion is judged 'P1'; Top-5 Accuracy = share judged P1 or P2..P5 ('P5' = GT contained within / broader term for any of the 5 predictions); judged by an LLM (GPT-4-0613) from the diagnosis text; denominator = cases with a parseable score.

original_values.RAMEDIS_counts: P1=107, P2-P5=29, P0=62 of 198 scored rows (2 of 200 rows carry malformed quoted scores and are excluded by the paper's counting) - recomputed from data/scores_RAMEDIS_gpt4turbo0409.csv

claim.original_source: Paper Table 3 (RAMEDIS, 200 cases), Table 5 (PUMCH, 75 cases), Table 1 (synthetic, 200 cases); all three reproduced exactly from repo score files data/scores_RAMEDIS_gpt4turbo0409.csv, data/scores_PUMCH_ADM_gpt4turbo0409.csv, data/scores_v2_gpt4turbo0409.csv using the counting in src/dashboard_scores.py

protocol.model_usage_verified: yes - src/batch_diagnosis_v2.py instantiates ChatOpenAI(model_name='gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09', temperature=0, max_tokens=800) and the paper labels it 'GPT-4 Turbo 0409'
protocol.endpoint: POST https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions (original via langchain ChatOpenAI, direct OpenAI key; GPT-4-0613/1106 arms used Azure deployments)
protocol.prompt_source: src/batch_diagnosis_v2.py PROMPT_TEMPLATE (identical text in paper Appendix 6 'Diagnostic prompt')

messages.content:
Behave like a hypotethical doctor who has to do a diagnosis for a patient. Give me a list of potential diseases with a short description. Shows for each potential diseases always with '

+' and a number, starting with '

+1', for example '

+23.' (never return 

-), the name of the disease and finish with ':'. Dont return '

-', return '

+' instead. You have to indicate which symptoms the patient has in common with the proposed disease and which symptoms the patient does not have in common. The text is 
 Symptoms:{description}

protocol.input_construction: RareBench RAMEDIS test split: 'Phenotype' = list of HPO ids mapped to HPO term names with pyhpo (Ontology.get_hpo_object(id).name); the Python list repr of the names is inserted as {description}. Ground truth = Orphanet preferred names resolved through api.orphacode.org (hard-coded apiKey 'f29dev') from ORPHA codes in 'RareDisease' (mapping_fn_with_hpo3_plus_orpha_api). The archived data/diagnoses_RAMEDIS_gpt4turbo0409.csv already contains GT strings and can be reused if the Orpha API is unavailable.

params.seed: not set; system_fingerprint to be logged
params.retries: 2 attempts per case in original code

protocol.evaluation: Automatic LLM-as-judge: for each case the GT and the full diagnosis text are placed in the evaluation prompt (src/diagnoses_analisis.py; paper Appendix 'Evaluation prompt') and an Azure deployment 'nav29' (GPT-4-0613 per paper Sections 2.4 and 4.4.2; temperature 0, max_tokens 800) returns 'P1', 'P5' or 'P0'. Strict = P1/(P1+P5+P0); Top-5 = (P1+P5)/(P1+P5+P0). No logprobs needed. Judge model is DEAD (gpt-4-0613 shut down 2024-09-13) -> a substitute judge must be used (see blockers/user_checks).
protocol.evaluation_prompt:
Behave like a medical doctor reviewing patient diagnoses. You will be given a Ground Truth diagnosis (GT) and 5 Predicted diagnoses (P1-P5). Compare the GT to the predictions and return a classification: 

    If GT exactly matches P1, return "P1".  
    If GT is contained within or is a broader term for P1-P5, return "P5".
    If GT does not match any of P1-P5, return "P0".

    The GT may be a more general diagnosis, while predictions may include specific conditions. Broadly match GT to any prediction it reasonably encompasses.
    ----------------------------------------
    The text is:

    GT: {gt}

    Predictions:

    {predictions} 
    ----------------------------------------
    Return either "P1", "P5", or "P0". Do not return any other text.
protocol.environment: Python: datasets (HF), pyhpo (HPO ontology download), pandas; Orphanet REST API for GT names; no code execution or GPU needed

blockers: Judge model is dead: the P1/P5/P0 scores were produced by GPT-4-0613 (Azure 'nav29'); re-execution requires a substitute judge. Mitigation built into this card: re-judge the ARCHIVED gpt-4-turbo-0409 diagnoses with the same substitute judge so that generator drift and judge drift are separable.
Ground-truth names come from a live Orphanet API with a hard-coded key; fall back to GT strings already stored in the archived diagnoses CSV.
RareBench license / redistribution terms not verified; our full-log archive will contain patient-derived HPO lists from RAMEDIS/PUMCH.
2 of 200 RAMEDIS rows have malformed judge outputs in the original; denominator 198 must be reproduced or documented.

baseline_alive.purpose: live baseline (P0); judge = substitute (proposed gpt-4o-2024-05-13, dying, or gpt-4.1)

budget.assumptions: RAMEDIS only: 200 cases x 3 seeds = 600 generation calls (~250 in / ~600 out tokens, max_tokens 800) = $12.3; judge: 600 new + 200 archived re-judge = 800 calls (~900 in / 5 out) = $3.7. Adding PUMCH (75 cases) costs ~+$6; adding the synthetic set ~+$16. Temperature 0 means seeds mostly measure API nondeterminism.

judgment.rule: ANALYSIS_PLAN section 1. Primary number: RAMEDIS Strict Accuracy (P1) of gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09. Survival = re-run P1 (median over 3 seeds, substitute judge) lies within the bootstrap 95% CI over the 200 cases of the archived-original P1 re-scored by the SAME substitute judge (judge-matched comparison), and Top-5 keeps the same direction (Top-5 > Strict by roughly 15 pp). Partial = P1 within CI of the paper's 54.04 but not of the judge-matched value (or vice versa). Death = P1 outside both CIs or Top-5 ordering reversed.
judgment.notes: Because the original judge is dead, the paper's published 54.04 can only be compared indirectly; report both the judge-matched comparison (primary) and the raw comparison to 54.04 (secondary). Cross-model ranking claims (Opus > Turbo-0409 > GPT-4-0613) are not testable since the comparators are dead.

user_checks: Accept the two-track design (re-judge archived originals + new generations with one substitute judge)? Which substitute judge: gpt-4o-2024-05-13 (dying, closest era) or gpt-4.1 (alive)?
Core claim = RAMEDIS Table 3 (real cases). OK, or should PUMCH (Table 5, 75 cases) / synthetic (Table 1) be added as secondary rows in the same run?
Confirm RareBench (HF chenxz/RareBench) license permits use and that archiving full request/response logs containing RAMEDIS/PUMCH HPO lists is acceptable.
Orphanet API: reuse GT strings from the archived diagnoses CSV instead of calling api.orphacode.org (avoids the hard-coded key)?
domain_notes: Inputs are HPO term lists (not narrative vignettes) and ground truths are Orphanet disease names, so the task is closer to phenotype-to-diagnosis retrieval than clinical reasoning. The 'P5' rule (GT is contained within or a broader term for a prediction) is lenient and highly judge-dependent; a domain reviewer should spot-check ~30 judged rows per arm for agreement with the original judge labels, which are archived. The preprint is not peer reviewed and uses the evaluator LLM's own family (GPT-4) as judge, a known bias the authors acknowledge (Section 4.4.2).
decisions_2026_09_18: two-track design accepted: re-judge the archived original diagnoses and judge the new generations with the same substitute judge, gpt-4o-2024-05-13
core claim = RAMEDIS Table 3 (200 real cases) only; PUMCH and synthetic cases are not run
RAMEDIS only (public case reports); if RareBench terms forbid redistribution the archive keeps item ids and hashes instead of item text
reuse the ground-truth strings from the archived diagnoses CSV; no Orphanet API call
